plan.melodySummary: The melody opens in the Clarinet's warm middle register, migrates to French Horn and Cello for inner-voice color, then blazes in Violin 1 at the fortissimo climax before settling back into the strings for a tender resolution. The dynamic arc breathes through repeated hairpins from an intimate piano, swelling steadily to a triumphant ff at mm.17-25, then receding to a lingering, espressivo pianissimo close.

sections.label: Phrase A
sections.notes: Sing the theme espressivo at !mp!, gently tapering each two-bar phrase with a soft hairpin; take a light breath before m.5.

sections.label: Phrase A'
sections.notes: Take the tune nobly at !mf!, slightly lingering on the tied notes in m.8 and m.12; project warmly over flowing string arpeggios.

sections.label: Phrase B
sections.notes: Play the theme in the rich tenor register at !mf!, molto espressivo; broaden into the D cadence at m.16 to launch the climb.

sections.label: Phrase B climax
sections.notes: Soar in the high octave, growing !f!→!ff!; broad ringing tone, sustain the tied g in m.20 at full intensity.

sections.label: Grand statement
sections.notes: Maintain the !ff! peak with brilliant, singing tone; give the arching phrase full Romantic breadth into m.25.

sections.label: Coda / Resolution
sections.notes: Recede from !mf! to a tender !pp! by m.32; molto espressivo, lingering rubato on the final tied cadence as all voices soften together.

Violin 1.instruction: Espressivo lyrical countermelody with soaring lines in early sections; take the fortissimo climactic melody at mm.17-25 with brilliant sustained tone, then fold back into shimmering countermelody, ending pianissimo.

Violin 2.instruction: Provide flowing broken-chord arpeggios and gently repeated chords supplying chromatic inner voices; shape every phrase with hairpins, always staying softer than the melody carrier.

Clarinet.instruction: Open the theme warmly at mp and close it with a tender pp; when not on melody, weave chromatic suspensions and expressive countermelody resolving downward into each cadence.

French Horn.instruction: State the theme nobly at mf in mm.7-12; elsewhere sustain rich harmonic pedals and warm countermelodies with secondary-dominant color, breathing with the strings.

Cello.instruction: Anchor the harmony with flowing arpeggiated bass lines and chromatic passing tones; sing the theme molto espressivo in the tenor register at mm.13-16, then return to a supportive, resonant bass.
